title_en: Beijing Zhongrui Culture Communication Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Lingdian Market Survey and Analysis Co., Ltd. — unfair competition dispute
keywords_en: civil; unfair competition dispute; first instance; intermediate people's court; Beijing; legal person; Anti-Unfair Competition Law; identification of trade secrets; scope of confidentiality obligations; concurrence of breach of contract and tort; partial support; market survey entrustment; disclosure of trade secrets; public release of investigation report; good faith; unfair competition; unfair competition dispute with analysis company
full_text_en:
Beijing Zhongrui Culture Communication Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Zero Point Market Research and Analysis Company — dispute over unfair competition

Plaintiff: Beijing Zhongrui Culture Communication Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Ren Jingxi, Manager

Agent ad litem: Peng Yan, Attorney at Beijing Zhengping Law Firm

Defendant: Beijing Zero Point Market Research and Analysis Company

Legal Representative: Yuan Yue, General Manager

Agent ad litem: Guo Mengzhen, Attorney at Beijing Horizon Law Firm

The plaintiff, Beijing Zhongrui Culture Communication Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongrui Company), filed a lawsuit with the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Beijing Zero Point Market Research and Analysis Company (hereinafter referred to as Zero Point Company), concerning a dispute over unfair competition.

The plaintiff alleged: The defendant, Zero Point Company, breached the agreement with our company by publicly disclosing our company's trade secrets through the media, causing significant economic losses to our company. We request the court to order the defendant to refund all entrusted investigation fees paid by our company, totaling RMB 13,124; to compensate for economic losses of RMB 318,000 caused by the breach of contract; to make a public apology to our company; and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The defendant, Zero Point Company, argued: Our company is a professional market research company that only publishes market research results or social surveys that we have invested in ourselves or that the client has requested to be made public. The survey article that the plaintiff alleges we published contains all data from our own research projects and from a publicly available consumer rights awareness research report conducted for the CCTV March 15 Program Team. None of the content comes from the research report commissioned by the plaintiff. Therefore, compared to the results of the plaintiff's commissioned survey, the article differs in research scope, research content, sample size, survey method, and research period. The plaintiff, unlike Western investors who pay high costs to exclusively purchase our survey service rights in a particular investment field, has no right to restrict our company from conducting similar research alone or for other clients and freely disposing of the research results. The plaintiff has no right to claim rights over the technical design layout of the commissioned research project, let alone prevent our company from publishing our own research results. The plaintiff's claims exceed the scope agreed upon in the agreement and should be dismissed. Our company has strictly performed the obligations under the agreement, while the plaintiff still owes the entrusted fees. In this regard, our company files a counterclaim, requesting the court to order the plaintiff to immediately pay the outstanding entrusted fees of RMB 15,410 and the liquidated damages of RMB 35,148 as of the date of the counterclaim.

The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found the following facts after trial:

On May 5, 1998, the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company (Party A under the agreement), and the defendant, Zero Point Company (Party B under the agreement), signed a Project Cooperation Agreement stipulating: Party A commissions Party B to conduct market research on the behavior patterns of urban households renting video products, for which Party A shall pay Party B an entrusted fee of RMB 38,540. This fee is to be prepaid at 30% on the date of signing, i.e., RMB 11,562; another 30% is to be paid on the day after the interviewer training; and the balance is to be paid within seven days after the report is delivered. Party A has exclusive ownership of all results obtained from this survey. Party B undertakes a confidentiality obligation regarding all results obtained by Party A in this survey and all commercial documents provided by Party A during the survey process. If Party A delays payment, it shall pay an additional penalty equal to 2% of the unpaid amount for each day of delay. If Party B fails to fulfill its confidentiality obligation, it shall refund all entrusted fees and provide a new survey free of charge. The specific matters of this survey are set out in the "Project Plan for Research on Urban Household Behavior Patterns of Renting Video Products," which was specially designed by Party B upon Party A's commission and confirmed by both parties. This plan, as an appendix to the agreement, is the basic standard for Party A to inspect the survey results and has the same effect as the terms of the agreement. The design copyright of the plan belongs to Party B and shall not be provided to competitors of the copyright owner without the consent of the copyright owner. The agreement also makes provisions for other related rights and obligations.

The plan, which serves as an appendix to the agreement, states that the purpose of the survey is "to understand the current consumption status, consumption behavior patterns, rental preferences, potential demand, and the choices and needs for services provided by rental venues of urban households regarding video products, primarily VCDs, so as to provide decision-making references for the client to position itself in the video product rental market, identify entry opportunities, and formulate investment plans." The plan also provides detailed provisions on research content, research methods, survey results, project schedule, project flowchart, and cost budget.

After the agreement was signed, the defendant, Zero Point Company, conducted the survey work as agreed and submitted to the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, at the end of June, the "Comprehensive Survey Report on the Urban Video Product Rental Market." The main findings of this report are as follows: 1. Urban households' psychological demand for video consumption. Conclusion: Video consumption is relatively important to consumers, but people are not very satisfied with the video consumption market. Video products play a significant role in people's cultural consumption expenditure, and most people indicate that their future video consumption expenditure will increase. This conclusion is based on survey results such as the status of household video consumption, the proportion of leisure time spent on video entertainment, and viewing time (frequency). 2. Urban households' consumption behavior patterns for video products (primarily VCDs). Conclusion: "Purchasing" and "borrowing" are the main channels for people to obtain video products, and the main factors influencing consumers' video consumption decisions are "friends" and "television." At the same time, people are most concerned about the price and retention value of video products. This conclusion is based on survey results such as the channels through which consumers obtain video products and possible changes in rental behavior in the coming year. 3. Current status of the video product rental market. Conclusion: People tend to patronize rental stores located near their residences and are more concerned about "movie quality," "rental fees," and "variety and richness of content" at rental stores. The evaluation of membership systems at rental stores is average, and people prefer direct discounts and service methods. This conclusion is based on survey results such as the proportion of various video products rented, the frequency and volume of VCD rentals. 4. Choices and needs for rentals. Based on survey results such as the likelihood of patronizing rental stores near residential areas, main considerations for choosing a rental store, and pricing for movie rentals. 5. Regarding the implementation of membership systems at video product rental stores. In the summary and recommendations section of this report, it clearly states: "Most people consider video consumption to be very necessary or relatively necessary for themselves, and respondents generally indicate that the proportion of expenditure on video consumption will increase in the future, indicating that the video market has considerable development prospects..." "The survey also found that the current video product rental market is relatively lacking, with rental stores rarely seen in most residential areas... For some video products (such as educational ones), the demand for purchase is greater than for rental. It is recommended to organically combine rental and sales services and content to create better economic benefits."

After signing the agreement, the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, paid the defendant, Zero Point Company, a total of RMB 33,124 in installments as agreed, with an outstanding balance of RMB 15,416. Before and after receiving the survey report from Zero Point Company, Zhongrui Company had prepared for investment in the VCD market by renting stores for opening. Subsequently, Zhongrui Company refused to pay the remaining amount under the agreement, claiming that Zero Point Company had disclosed the survey results, causing it losses. The parties failed to reach a settlement through negotiation, leading to the lawsuit.

It was also found that: From January to March 1998, the defendant, Zero Point Company, independently completed a market survey report on the rental behavior patterns of video products among Beijing urban residents. The introduction of that report states that the VCD market was very lively in 1997, and to understand the market situation of video product rental chain stores, Zero Point Company conducted this research, hoping to outline a general picture of the currently very active video product rental market. The main findings of that report are: 1. The position of video products in living spaces; 2. Video product rental behavior. The key findings include: Beijing residents spend an average of about one hour per day at home watching TV or VCDs to pass their leisure time, go out to watch movies or videos less than twice a month, and generally prefer watching popular blockbusters and entertainment programs... In terms of sources for consumers to watch video products, the volume of rentals is greater than purchases. Generally, consumers keep rented video products at home for about one day... The volume of video product rentals by consumers is expected to increase in the next one to two years... The vast majority of consumers are relatively interested in target video product rental stores... In addition, in March 1998, Zero Point Company was commissioned by the 315 Program Team of the Economics Department of CCTV to conduct a comprehensive test of Chinese urban consumers' awareness of rights and interests and issued a report, which included a survey on the issue of "VCD" piracy. On June 16, 1998, Zero Point Company published an article titled "Where to Find VCDs in Beijing?" in the "First Hand" weekly magazine. The article states: ...If he goes to bed at 11 o'clock, then he spends almost all of his remaining evening time watching TV or VCDs... If ordinary residents spend so much time watching VCDs, they will have considerable expenses in the future. Thus, discs become a headache for VCD machine consumers... Survey results show that currently, Beijing residents have three sources for watching video products (in this survey, video products mainly refer to VCDs, hereinafter the same concept): purchase, rent, and borrow... The volume obtained through purchase is the smallest, averaging 8.76 items per household; borrowing is in the middle at 23.13 items; and renting is the largest at 31.41 items. The volume of video rentals by consumers will increase in the next one to two years... The article also published and commented on content such as "Will the video products in your hands be transferred?", "Which are your favorites?", and "Are you satisfied?"

The above facts are confirmed by three survey reports, original survey questionnaires, a copy of Issue 25 of the "First Hand" weekly, a comparison table prepared by both parties, and witness testimony.

The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held:

Currently, there are no uniform regulations in China governing market research practices. Therefore, the agreement between the parties serves as the primary basis for regulating the rights and obligations of both parties and resolving this dispute. International customary practices and established industry norms may serve as references for handling this case.

The first issue in this case is: What is the scope of confidentiality agreed upon in the agreement between the parties, i.e., what does the broadly stated "all results obtained from this survey" refer to? Considering the content of the agreement and the research purpose, method, conclusions, etc., stated in the project plan, and comparing it with the already completed "Comprehensive Survey Report on the Urban Video Product Rental Market," it can be determined that the survey data and conclusions involved in the report constitute the confidential content agreed upon in the agreement. According to the agreement, the defendant, Zero Point Company, is obligated to keep this content confidential.

The second issue in this case is: Whether the information published by the defendant, Zero Point Company, in the "First Hand" weekly constitutes an infringement of the plaintiff Zhongrui Company's trade secrets. Pursuant to paragraph 3 of Article 10 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the content that Zhongrui Company requires to be kept confidential is of practical use to practitioners in the VCD industry and can bring economic benefits to the right holder, and therefore constitutes a trade secret of the company. It is undeniable that Zero Point Company had conducted similar market surveys on the VCD market before accepting Zhongrui Company's commission. Some of the data and information published in the "First Hand" weekly originate from these survey reports. However, this published information happens to be identical to Zhongrui Company's trade secrets. By publishing these results, Zero Point Company undoubtedly disclosed a commercial message to the general public or other VCD operators, thereby revealing Zhongrui Company's trade secrets and breaching its contractual obligations.

The third issue in this case is: Whether the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, "exclusively purchased" the defendant, Zero Point Company's, right to provide survey services in the VCD market? As Zero Point Company argues, "exclusive purchase" refers to an explicit agreement between Western investors and a survey company at a high price, stipulating that the survey company's research in a particular investment field can only serve that investor. The agreement signed by the parties in this case contains no such stipulation. As a professional survey company, Zero Point Company is well aware of the industry's practices. When signing the contract, it should have acted in good faith and had an obligation to inform the other party of the industry practices, so that the other party could decide whether it needed to "exclusively purchase" the survey service rights. Zero Point Company failed to fulfill this disclosure obligation and should bear the liability for pre-contractual fault. Even if Zero Point Company were allowed to conduct surveys in the same field on its own or on behalf of others and provide services, doing so would inevitably give rise to conflicts of interest with clients. According to recognized commercial ethics, a survey company should also keep information concerning clients' interests confidential. If it wishes to disclose such information, it must obtain the client's consent. Zero Point Company, without the consent of the right holder or interested party, arbitrarily disclosed relevant confidential information. This conduct contravenes the provisions of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, which states that "business operators shall, in their market transactions, follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, honesty and good faith, and abide by recognized commercial ethics." Such conduct falls under the unfair competition practices prohibited by subparagraph (3) of paragraph 1 of Article 10 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

In summary, the defendant, Zero Point Company, as a professional survey company, frequently conducts market surveys on behalf of clients and is generally privy to clients' commercial information. It should strictly adhere to recognized commercial ethics and the agreements of the parties in providing services. The unfair competition conduct of Zero Point Company in this case has caused certain losses to the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, and it should bear corresponding civil liability. However, the compensation amount claimed by Zhongrui Company is excessive. The court will determine the amount of compensation within the scope of the agreed entrusted fees, market operation reinvestment, and actual litigation expenses. The counterclaim of Zero Point Company lacks legal basis and is not supported. The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 17, 1998:

1. The defendant, Zero Point Company, shall, within 15 days after this judgment takes effect, refund the entrusted fees to and compensate for other economic losses of the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, totaling RMB 100,000.
2. Within one month after this judgment takes effect, the defendant, Zero Point Company, shall publish an apology to the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, in a nationwide newspaper. The content of the apology letter must be approved by the court (if not performed within the time limit, the court will publish the judgment content in a nationwide newspaper, and the expenses incurred shall be borne by Zero Point Company).
3. The other claims of the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, are rejected.
4. The counterclaim of the defendant, Zero Point Company, is rejected.

Court acceptance fee for the original action: RMB 7,627, to be borne by the plaintiff, Zhongrui Company, in the amount of RMB 1,000, and by the defendant, Zero Point Company, in the amount of RMB 6,627. Court acceptance fee for the counterclaim: RMB 2,040, to be borne by Zero Point Company.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party filed an appeal.
